title: Signed Koszul dual homology and evaluated derived morphisms
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq 0$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$. Let $K=K_A(f)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], $E$ its integer extension with $K_n$ in degree $-n$, and $L$ its signed dual [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex]. In the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there exists an $A$-linear equivalence $e:\operatorname{Hom}(Q(E),Q(A[-r]))\cong H^r(L)$ such that for every complex map $z:E\to A[-r]$ and every cycle $y$ of $L$ in degree $r$ whose image under the cycle inclusion is the degree $-r$ component of $z$ transported to $\operatorname{Hom}_A(K_r,A)$ by extendXIso.inv and singleObjXSelf.hom, one has $e(Q(z))=\operatorname{homologyPi}(y)$. There is no ideal, regularity or augmentation hypothesis.

source.place: lemma-regular-immersion-ext, local computation by the Hom complex of the finite free Koszul complex; component and quotient details supplied by Mathlib HomComplexSingle, HomComplexCohomology and DerivedCategory/KProjective

proof.text: Give each term of K its exterior basis [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. Its integer extension E is K-projective by the natural-number extension instance of [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective]. The comparison [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] identifies derived morphisms from E with homotopy classes of complex maps.

Put T=single(A,-r) and S=L.sc r. For each x in ker(S.g), the outgoing signed differential equation and the unit sign imply d_(r+1,r) followed by x.val equals zero. Transport x.val by extendXIso.hom and form the degree-zero cocycle C(x)=Cocycle.toSingleMk with target T, using the extend_d_eq equation. Its actual complex map is Cocycle.homOf(C(x)). Define F(x)=Q.map of this map. Component evaluation and single-map extensionality prove additivity and A-linearity. Every derived map lifts to z by K-projectivity; Cocycle.toSingleMk_surjective applied to Cocycle.ofHom(z) and transport back to K_r produce x. Its cycle condition follows from the chain-map equation returned by Cocycle.toSingleMk_surjective, transported by extend_d_eq and cancellation of extendXIso.hom; the signed dual differential is the unit sign times this zero composite. Hence F(x)=Q(z). Thus F is surjective.

Prove Q.map(z)=0 iff z is null-homotopic, by Qh_map_bijective injectivity and the quotientCompQhIso naturality equation. Cochain.equivHomotopy and mem_coboundaries_iff then give Q.map(Cocycle.homOf(C(x)))=0 iff C(x) is a coboundary. By Cocycle.toSingleMk_mem_coboundaries_iff this means x.val is precomposition by the differential from K_r to K_(r-1). For r>0 transport the witness using extendXIso in degree r-1. Multiply it by (-1)^r to obtain a signed-dual boundary; conversely a signed-dual boundary gives a cochain witness by the same sign, since its square is 1. For r=0 the witness has source E^1=0, hence x.val=0, and S.f is zero by the shape identity. In all cases ker(F)=range(S.moduleCatToCycles). These are the concrete single-target cocycle and homotopy-quotient formulas.

Form q=F.quotKerEquivOfSurjective, identify ker(F) with range(S.moduleCatToCycles) by the proved equality, and use S.moduleCatHomologyIso.toLinearEquiv to define d:H^r(L) -> Hom_D(Q(E),Q(T)); take e=d.symm. For a supplied y with the evaluation of z, let x=S.moduleCatCyclesIso.hom(y). moduleCatCyclesIso_hom_i identifies x.val with the supplied evaluation, so single-map extensionality proves Cocycle.homOf(C(x))=z. The projection identity pi_moduleCatCyclesIso_hom identifies the image of homologyPi(y) with the quotient class of x. The quotient-equivalence projection formula gives d(homologyPi(y))=F(x)=Q(z). Injectivity of d and d.apply_symm_apply give the required e(Q(z))=homologyPi(y).

proof_origin.place: B3 complete Lean proof: linear map from the kernel to derived morphisms, surjectivity via K-projectivity, kernel=image via single-target coboundary formulas, and quotient projection compatibility. Repair: the lifting helper is generalized to every K-projective complex. No top-differential vanishing helper is used: lifted functionals are cycles directly by their chain-map equation.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_koszul_derived_dual_evaluation
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) :
    ∃ e : (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((koszulComplex A r f).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat) ⟶
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat A) (-(r : ℤ))).obj
              (ModuleCat.of A A))) ≃ₗ[A] (koszulDualComplex A r f).homology r,
      ∀ z : (koszulComplex A r f).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ⟶
          (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat A) (-(r : ℤ))).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A A),
        ∀ y : (koszulDualComplex A r f).cycles r,
          (koszulDualComplex A r f).iCycles r y =
            ((koszulComplex A r f).extendXIso
              ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat (i := r) rfl).inv ≫ z.f (-(r : ℤ)) ≫
                (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (-(r : ℤ))
                  (ModuleCat.of A A)).hom →
          e (DerivedCategory.Q.map z) = (koszulDualComplex A r f).homologyπ r y
